body: On 24 Jan 2023, as Adani Enterprises launched a Rs 20,000 cr FPO, Hindenburg Research alleged stock manipulation and accounting fraud via Mauritius-linked offshore entities, concealed related parties and high leverage, and said seven listed group stocks had ~85% downside on fundamentals. Group market value fell >$100 bn within ~10 days (peak loss ~$150 bn); Adani Enterprises fell ~60%+ from ~Rs 3,400 to ~Rs 1,017 (3 Feb 2023); the fully subscribed FPO was withdrawn on 1 Feb. Partial recovery followed (GQG's $1.9 bn investment Mar 2023; Supreme Court expert committee May 2023 found no regulatory failure; SC Jan 2024 declined further probes). Nov 2024 US DOJ/SEC charges (bribery-related, Adani Green) were a separate shock. Hindenburg shut down in Jan 2025. On 18 Sep 2025 SEBI's final orders closed the related-party allegations (Adicorp, Milestone Tradelinks, Rehvar) with no penalties, holding the transactions were not RPTs under the pre-2021 definition; separate MPS/insider-trading matters were reported as still under examination. Visible-in-advance (pre-report) flags: very high P/E/P/B on capital-intensive businesses, net debt/EBITDA high in several companies, concentrated offshore FPI holders and low free float, small audit firms for large companies, earlier promoter pledges. Lesson: a short report is an allegation, not a verdict; but valuation + leverage + float concentration alone can create a -60% drawdown regardless of the legal outcome. Size positions so a contested governance event is survivable.

data.early_signals: extreme valuations; leverage; concentrated offshore holders; small auditors; low float
data.lesson: Allegation != verdict, but fragility drives drawdown; position-size
data.outcome_2025: SEBI 18-Sep-2025: RPT allegations closed, no penalty; other probes reported pending
data.spotted_by: Hindenburg Research (Nate Anderson); earlier CreditSights 'deeply overleveraged' note Aug 2022

title: Adani-Hindenburg (Jan 2023) and SEBI's Sep 2025 orders
